title: Checking the heart: pulse and ECG
examples: How fast should my heart beat when I run?
What is the difference between a pulse and an ECG?
Can you show me where to feel my pulse?

explain.say: Today we are learning about checking the heart. We will look at heart rate, pulse points, and the ECG trace.

draw.text: Checking the heart: pulse and ECG
Heart Rate, Pulse Points, ECG Trace

explain.say: First we learn about heart rate. This is how many times your heart beats in one minute. A normal resting rate is usually between sixty and one hundred beats per minute.
Next we look at pulse points. You can feel your pulse at specific spots on your body. A common place is at your wrist, which is called the radial artery.
The ECG trace shows the heart's electrical activity. It records the electrical signals that cause your heart to beat. This trace is drawn on a piece of paper.
In real life, a doctor uses these checks. They measure your pulse to check your heart rate. They might also use an ECG machine to check your rhythm.
A common mistake is thinking pulse equals heart rate. Remember, the pulse is just a feeling, while the heart rate is a measured count over time.

draw.text: Pulse reading is not heart rate

faq.q: What exactly does an ECG machine measure?
faq.a: An ECG machine measures the electrical signals that travel through your heart muscle. These signals tell doctors how well your heart is beating electrically.
asks: What is the purpose of an ECG?

faq.q: Is it normal to have a high pulse rate?
faq.a: It can be normal if you have just exercised or are very nervous. However, if it stays high when you are resting, a doctor should check it.
asks: When is a fast pulse normal?
What causes a high heart rate?

faq.q: Where exactly on my wrist should I check my pulse?
faq.a: You should place two fingers gently on the inner side of your wrist. You are feeling the pulse where the radial artery runs close to the bone.
asks: How do I take my pulse?
Which artery do I check for a pulse?

faq.q: What does the rhythm on an ECG look like?
faq.a: A normal rhythm shows regular, consistent waves. Irregular patterns can suggest the heart is beating in a way that needs attention.
asks: What is a normal heart rhythm?
What does an abnormal ECG look like?

faq.q: Can I measure my heart rate accurately by just counting my pulse?
faq.a: You can get an estimate, but a proper count over a full minute is best. Doctors use specialized equipment for the most accurate reading.
asks: What is the best way to count beats?

facts: The heart beats due to electrical impulses.
Pulse points allow us to estimate heart rate.
The ECG records the heart's electrical activity on paper.
Resting heart rates are usually between sixty and one hundred beats per minute.

quiz.say: If a person's heart beats 110 times in one minute while sitting still, what is this called?
quiz.why: Tachycardia means a heart rate that is too fast for the resting state.

wrong.0: This describes the pattern, not the speed itself.
wrong.2: This term means the heart rate is too slow, which is the opposite.
wrong.3: A pulse check is just feeling the beat, not measuring the rate.

quiz.say: When checking a pulse at the wrist, which artery are you feeling?
quiz.why: The radial artery is the main artery easily felt on the inner wrist side.

wrong.0: This artery is located much lower, in the groin area.
wrong.1: This is a vein, not an artery where you check pulse.
wrong.3: This artery is felt in the neck, not the wrist.

quiz.say: What does the P wave on an ECG trace represent?
quiz.why: The P wave shows the electrical signal starting the atria to contract.

wrong.0: This is represented by the larger QRS complex waves.
wrong.1: This is a circulatory function, not the electrical trace shown.
wrong.2: The trace shows activity, not just a period of rest.
